Implement output classifiers to detect out-of-scope model behaviour

mitigations: Implement per-client rate limiting on model inference endpoints
Set maximum token limits per request to prevent expensive queries
Configure compute resource limits (CPU/GPU quotas) per model instance
Monitor inference latency and alert on abnormal resource consumption
Implement query complexity scoring to reject expensive inputs

threats.description: 'tools' (tool-executor) has no integrity verification defined. Malicious code in libraries or modules used by this AI framework component can compromise its functionality, leading to unexpected results and potentially malicious behavior from the AI agent.
mitigations: Implement cryptographic integrity verification on all framework components
Use signed package verification for all framework dependencies
Pin framework component versions to verified, known-good releases
Monitor framework component checksums and alert on changes

threats.subcategory: No Dependency Verification on Framework — Supply Chain Attack Risk
threats.description: 'tools' (tool-executor) has no dependency verification defined. An attacker can target the AI framework's upstream dependencies, compromising software before delivery and distribution and resulting in compromised AI agent software without the operator's knowledge.
mitigations: Implement software bill of materials (SBOM) for all framework dependencies
Use dependency scanning tools to detect known vulnerabilities
Lock dependency versions and verify checksums on every build
Use a private package registry to control approved dependencies
Monitor upstream packages for unexpected changes or new versions

threats.subcategory: No Output Filtering on Framework — Framework Evasion Risk
threats.description: 'tools' (tool-executor) has no output filtering defined. AI agents can use advanced techniques to bypass security controls within the framework, producing outputs that perform unauthorized actions outside the agent's intended scope.
mitigations: Implement output filtering on all framework component outputs
Define explicit security controls that cannot be bypassed by agent outputs
Use a separate security enforcement layer independent of the framework
Regularly test framework security controls with adversarial agent prompts
Monitor agent outputs for patterns indicative of evasion attempts

threats.subcategory: No Rate Limiting or Resource Limits on Framework — DoS Risk
threats.description: 'llm-generate' (llm) has no rate limiting or resource limits defined. An attacker can disrupt the AI framework's ability to function by overloading its services, preventing normal operation of the AI agents that depend on this framework component.
mitigations: Implement rate limiting on all framework API endpoints
Define resource consumption limits per request and per session
Implement circuit breakers to prevent cascading failures
Monitor framework API usage and alert on abnormal load patterns

Use policy-as-code tools (e.g. OPA, Checkov) to validate IaC before apply
Enforce code review and approval workflows for all IaC changes
Store IaC in version-controlled repositories with branch protection
Audit IaC pipelines for unauthorized modifications

threats.subcategory: No Resource Limits on Infrastructure — DoS Attack Risk

mitigations: Define CPU, memory, and network resource limits for all AI infrastructure components
Implement auto-scaling with hard upper bounds to prevent resource exhaustion
Use rate limiting at the infrastructure layer to prevent request flooding
Implement circuit breakers to isolate overloaded components
Monitor infrastructure resource usage and alert on anomalous consumption

Maintain an audit trail of all security decisions made by AI agents
